record.title: Average-distance conjecture for touching Jordan curves
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a $k$-touching family of Jordan curves, meaning that no point of the plane lies on more than $k$ curves. For each pair of intersecting curves $a,b\in\mathcal{F}$, let $d(a,b)$ be the number of curves whose bounded region contains exactly one of $a$ and $b$, and define the average distance in $\mathcal{F}$ as the average of $d(a,b)$ over all intersecting pairs.

**Average-distance conjecture.** For any $k$-touching family $\mathcal{F}$ of Jordan curves, the average distance in $\mathcal{F}$ is at most

$$
\frac{k}{2}.
$$

The conjecture concerns possibly nonsimple families of touching Jordan curves, in which two curves may intersect at several points. The supplied source text gives no resolution evidence for this claim; its status is therefore open.
record.source_name: Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Louis Esperet and Tobias Müller, “Coloring Jordan regions and curves”, arXiv:1608.08159 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.08159

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2016). “It was proved by Fox and Pach that each $k$-touching family of strings is $(6ek+1)$-colorable, which directly implies that each $k$-touching family of Jordan curves is $(6ek+1)$-colorable (note that $6e\approx 16.31$).”

record.title: The period-one classification for partial chess pieces
record.statement: Let a partial queen $\mathbb Q^{hk}$ be a chess piece with $h$ horizontal or vertical basic moves and $k$ diagonal basic moves, where $h,k\leq 2$. **Period-one classification conjecture.** The rook, semirook, semibishop, and subqueen are the only four pieces among these partial queens whose counting functions are polynomials in $n$, equivalently whose counting quasipolynomials have period $1$. The table records this as a conjectural classification; no general proof is supplied.
record.source_name: Seth Chaiken, Christopher R. H. Hanusa and Thomas Zaslavsky, “A q-Queens Problem. V. Some of Our Favorite Pieces: Queens, Bishops, Rooks, and Nightriders”, arXiv:1609.00853 (2020).

record.title: The distinguishing stability bound for simple connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple connected graph. Write $D(G)$ for its distinguishing number and $st_D(G)$ for its distinguishing stability, namely the least number of vertices whose deletion changes the distinguishing number.

**Distinguishing stability conjecture.**

$$
st_D(G)\leqslant D(G)+1.
$$

The authors state this bound because it holds for the examples they have considered, but report that attempts to prove it have failed. Its general validity remains open.
record.source_name: Saeid Alikhani and Samaneh Soltani, “Stabilizing on the distinguishing number of a graph”, arXiv:1609.07345 (2016).

record.title: Mou and Pasechnik's Hamiltonicity conjecture for tough $2K_2$-free graphs
record.statement:
A graph is **$2K_2$-free** if it has no induced subgraph consisting of two independent edges, and it is **$t$-tough** if $|S|\geq t\,c(G-S)$ whenever deletion of $S$ leaves at least two components. A graph is **hamiltonian** if it has a spanning cycle.

**Mou and Pasechnik's conjecture.** Every $2$-tough $2K_2$-free graph with at least three vertices is hamiltonian.

The source presents this as one of two conjectures proposed by Mou and Pasechnik and gives no resolution for it here.
record.source_name: Guantao Chen, M. N. Ellingham, Akira Saito and Songling Shan, “Spanning trails with maximum degree at most 4 in 2K_2-free graphs”, arXiv:1609.08730 (2016).

record.title: Conjecture on the weight of maximal $(s,ms-1,ms+1)$-core partitions
record.statement:
Let $s$ and $m$ be positive integers, and let $t$ be determined by either $s=2t-1$ or $s=2t-2$. A maximal $(s,ms-1,ms+1)$-core partition is a core partition maximal under inclusion, and its size is its weight. **The maximal-core weight conjecture.** The size of a maximal $(s,ms-1,ms+1)$-core is

$$
\frac{m^2t(t-1)(t^2-t+1)}{6}
$$

if $s=2t-1$, and

$$
\frac{m^2(t-1)^2(t^2-2t+3)}{6}-\frac{m(t-1)^2}{2}
$$

if $s=2t-2$. There are two such maximal partitions, one corresponding to ${\mathcal L}(s)$ and one to its conjugate. This conjecture extends the agreement, when $m=1$, between the weight of a maximal $(s,ms-1,ms+1)$-core partition and the longest such core; the cited prior results concern the case $m=1$, while the general assertion remains unresolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Rishi Nath and James A. Sellers, “Abaci structures of (s,ms1)-core partitions”, arXiv:1610.01686 (2016).
record.references:

record.title: Naserasr's projective-hypercube conjecture for planar graphs
record.statement: Let $PC(2k)$ be the projective hypercube of dimension $2k$, obtained from the $(2k+1)$-dimensional hypercube by identifying antipodal vertices. A graph $H$ **bounds** the class of planar graphs of odd-girth at least $2k+1$ if every such planar graph admits a homomorphism to $H$. **Naserasr's conjecture.** The projective hypercube $PC(2k)$ bounds the class of planar graphs of odd-girth at least $2k+1$. Since $PC(2)$ is isomorphic to $K_4$, the first case is the Four-Colour Theorem; the conjecture also proposes an optimal bound in the corresponding odd-girth problem. Its general cases remain open.

record.title: The equality of the generalized sums $\tilde{S}_{k,j}(n)$ and $S_{k,j}(n)$
record.statement:
Let $x_r:=r^{2k+1}$, let $C_{j,q}(n)$ be the coefficients defined by the paper, and define

$$
s_{k,j}(n):=\sum_{q=0}^{j(n-1)}C_{j,q}(n)x_{j+q}.
$$

For integers $j\geq 1$, let

$$
\tilde{S}_{k,j}(n):=\sum_{\{\lambda\}\in B_{j,jn}}\left\{\lambda_1^{2k+1}+(\lambda_2-n)^{2k+1}+\cdots+(\lambda_j-jn+n)^{2k+1}\right\},
$$

where $B_{j,jn}:=\{\lambda_k:1\leq\lambda_1\leq\cdots\leq\lambda_j\leq jn\}$, and set

$$
S_{k,j}(n):=\sum_{q=0}^{j-1}{j(n+1)\choose q}s_{k,j-q}(n).
$$

**The generalized-sums equality.** For any $k\geq 0$ and $j\geq 1$, one has

$$
\tilde{S}_{k,j}(n)=S_{k,j}(n).
$$

The equality is proved in the paper for the particular case $j=2$, while the general case is presented as a conjecture.
record.source_name: Andrei K. Svinin, “Conjectures involving a generalization of the sums of powers of integers”, arXiv:1610.05387 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.05387

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2016).

record.title: The polynomial form of $S_{k,j}(n)$
record.statement:
Let $t:=n(n+1)$, and define

$$
g_1(n):=1,\qquad g_j(n):=\frac{j}{(j-1)!}\prod_{q=1}^{j-1}(jn+q)\quad (j\geq 2).
$$

**Polynomial-factorization conjecture.** There exist polynomials $P_k(t,x)$ in $x$ of degree $k$, with coefficients rationally depending on $t$, such that

$$
S_{k,j}(n)=\frac{t^{k+1}}{2^{k+1}}\left.P_k(t,x)\right|_{x=j}g_j(n).
$$

The conjecture is the paper's main conjecture for the general sums; the source records explicit examples through $k=7$ and notes that no recursion relation is known in general, although specialization at $t=2$ recovers Tuenter's polynomials.
record.source_name: Andrei K. Svinin, “Conjectures involving a generalization of the sums of powers of integers”, arXiv:1610.05387 (2017).

record.title: The coefficient-shape conjecture for $P_k(t,x)$
record.statement:
Write

$$
P_k(t,x)=x\left(p_{k,0}(t)x^{k-1}-p_{k,1}(t)x^{k-2}+\cdots+(-1)^{k-1}p_{k,k-1}(t)\right).
$$

Thus $p_{k,j}(t)$ denotes the coefficient functions in this expansion. **Coefficient-shape conjecture.** The coefficients satisfy

$$
p_{k,j}(t)=\frac{r_{k,j}(t)}{t^j},
$$

where

$$
r_{k,j}(t)=\sum_{q=0}^{m}\alpha_{k,j,q}t^{2q}(t+1)^{j-3q},
$$

with rational positive nonzero numbers $\alpha_{k,j,q}$; here $m\geq 0$ and $j=3m+l$ for some remainder $l$ on division of $j$ by $3$. The claim is based on calculations of the displayed polynomials $P_k(t,x)$; no proof or resolution is given in the source.
record.source_name: Andrei K. Svinin, “Conjectures involving a generalization of the sums of powers of integers”, arXiv:1610.05387 (2017).

record.title: The cluster-count criterion for secant and initial ideals
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a binary phylogenetic $[n]$-tree. For each $k$, let $c_k$ denote the number of $k$-clusters in $\mathcal{T}$, and let $J_{\mathcal{T}}$, $I_{2,n}$, $\omega$, and $\tau$ be as above, with

$$
J_{\mathcal{T}}=\tau\cdot \operatorname{in}_{\omega}(I_{2,n}).
$$

**The cluster-count criterion.** One has

$$
\tau\cdot \operatorname{in}_{\omega}\left(I_{2,n}^{\{r\}}\right)=J_{\mathcal{T}}^{\{r\}}
$$

if and only if

$$
\sum_{k=2}^{r}(r-k+1)c_k<2r^2-2r.
$$

This proposed modification is motivated by dimension bounds and examples showing failure of equality when the cluster-count expression is too large. The supplied text does not state whether the criterion has been proved or disproved.

record.title: Positivity conjecture for differences along the threshold-graph poset
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}_n$ be the poset of connected threshold graphs with vertices $0,1,\ldots,n$, ordered by subgraph inclusion: $H\preceq G$ when $H$ is a subgraph of $G$. For threshold graphs $G\succeq H$ in $\mathcal{P}_n$, **poset-difference positivity conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{Ehr}_{q,t}({\mathcal{F}}_G)-\operatorname{Ehr}_{q,t}({\mathcal{F}}_H)\in\mathbf{N}[q,t].
$$

The poset is isomorphic to the poset of shifted Young diagrams contained in $(n-1,n-2,\ldots,0)$. Computations up to $n=9$ suggest positivity along its cover relations; the conjecture as stated concerns all comparable threshold graphs.

record.title: Potts internal-energy bounds for regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $d$-regular graph, let $q\ge 2$, and let $\beta>0$. Write $K_{d,d}$ for the complete $d$-regular bipartite graph and $K_{d+1}$ for the complete graph on $d+1$ vertices. The internal energy and free energy per particle are denoted by $U^q_G(\beta)$ and $F^q_G(\beta)$, respectively.

**Regular-graph Potts bounds.** The conjectured inequalities are

$$
U^q_{K_{d,d}}(\beta)\le U^q_G(\beta)\le U^q_{K_{d+1}}(\beta),
$$

and, in particular,

$$
F^q_{K_{d+1}}(\beta)\le F^q_G(\beta)\le F^q_{K_{d,d}}(\beta).
$$

These bounds extend the theorem proved in the paper for cubic graphs; the case $d=2$ is stated to follow by direct calculation, while the higher-regularity case remains conjectural.

record.title: The Pin(2)-monopole Floer spectral sequence conjecture for branched double covers
record.statement:
Let $L\subset S^3$ be a link, let $\Sigma(L)$ denote its branched double cover, and let $\bar{L}$ be the mirror of $L$. Write $\widetilde{\mathrm{BN}}^3_{*,*}(\bar{L})$ for the relevant characteristic-two Bar-Natan homology and $\widetilde{\mathit{HS}}_*(\Sigma(L))$ for Pin(2)-monopole Floer homology. **Pin(2)-monopole Floer spectral sequence conjecture.** There exists a spectral sequence whose $E^2$-page is

$$
\widetilde{\mathrm{BN}}^3_{*,*}(\bar{L})
$$

which converges to

$$
\widetilde{\mathit{HS}}_*(\Sigma(L)).
$$

After setting $u$ equal to $Q$, this is a spectral sequence of $\mathbb{F}[Q]/Q^3$-modules. The conjecture proposes the Pin(2) analogue of the involutive monopole Floer spectral sequence established in the paper; the supplied text does not state that it has been resolved.

record.title: The equirepresentation matching conjecture for K_{n,n}
record.statement:
Let the edge set of $K_{n,n}$ be partitioned into sets $E_1,\ldots,E_n$, each of size $n$. A **matching** is a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges. **Equirepresentation matching conjecture.** There exists a matching in $K_{n,n}$ containing one edge from all but possibly one of the sets $E_i$.

This is identified in the paper as a special case of the fair perfect matching conjecture and is related to the Brualdi–Stein conjecture; the source does not report a resolution.
record.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Noga Alon, Eli Berger, Maria Chudnovsky, Dani Kotlar, Martin Loebl and Ran Ziv, “Fair representation by independent sets”, arXiv:1611.03196 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.03196

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2016). “This is proved in if $s$ is any power of $2$.”

record.title: Aharoni–Zerbib's conjecture for generalized $(k-1)$-covers
record.statement:
For $m<k$, let $\mathcal H(k,m)$ be the family of hypergraphs obtained by taking all $m$-subsets of the edges of a $k$-uniform hypergraph, and let

$$
h(k,m)=\sup\left\{\frac{\tau(J)}{\nu(J)}\mid J\in\mathcal H(k,m)\right\}.
$$

**Aharoni–Zerbib's conjecture for generalized $(k-1)$-covers.**

$$
h(k,k-1)=\left\lceil\frac{k+1}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

This predicts the exact covering-to-matching ratio in the case of $(k-1)$-subsets. The source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Ron Aharoni and Shira Zerbib, “A generalization of Tuza's conjecture”, arXiv:1611.07497 (2019).

record.title: Extension-language separation conjecture for prefix normal words
record.statement:
Let $v,w\in 1\{0,1\}^*$ be distinct prefix normal binary words. For each $m\geq 1$, let $\textit{ext}(v,m)$ and $\textit{ext}(w,m)$ denote the numbers of length-$m$ extensions that produce prefix normal words. **Extension-language separation conjecture.** If $v\neq w$, then the infinite sequences

$$
(\textit{ext}(v,m))_{m\geq 1}\quad\text{and}\quad(\textit{ext}(w,m))_{m\geq 1}
$$

are different. The preceding lemma establishes separation of the extension languages themselves; whether their growth, or equivalently these counting sequences, always differs was left unresolved.

record.title: Stapledon decomposition conjecture for graph polynomials
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $d$ vertices, and let $h_G(z)$ denote its associated polynomial. A decomposition of $h_G(z)$ uses polynomials $a(z)$ and $b(z)$ satisfying the displayed symmetry conditions.

**Stapledon decomposition conjecture.** The polynomial $h_G(z)$ can be decomposed as

$$
h_G(z)=a(z)+zb(z),
$$

where

$$
a(z)=z^{d}a\left(\frac{1}{z}\right),\qquad b(z)=z^{d-1}b\left(\frac{1}{z}\right),
$$

and $b(z)$ and $-a(z)$ have nonnegative coefficients.

The paper presents this as a conjectural strengthening of the coefficient inequalities previously proved for $h_G(z)$. It is motivated by decomposing the contributions from the order polytopes associated with acyclic orientations of $G$; the source reports computer experimentation but gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Emerson León, “Stapledon Decompositions and Inequalities for Coefficients of Chromatic Polynomials”, arXiv:1611.09728 (2016).

record.title: Conjecture on highly valenced graphs with two main and two plain eigenvalues
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a connected **$t$-valenced graph**, meaning that it has $t$ distinct valencies, with two main and two plain eigenvalues.

**Valency conjecture.** There exists a positive integer $C$ such that if $t\geq C$, then $\Gamma$ is a strong graph.

This conjecture is posed as an analogue of a question of de Caen about the number of distinct valencies in connected graphs with three distinct eigenvalues. The source gives no resolution of the conjecture.

record.title: The three-color pseudo-disk arrangement conjecture
record.statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a **pseudo-disk arrangement**, meaning a family of planar bodies whose boundaries are Jordan curves and such that the boundary of any member intersects the boundary of any other member in a connected curve. Let $S$ be a finite set of points. **The pseudo-disk arrangement conjecture.** Any finite set of points admits a $3$-coloring such that every pseudo-disk in the arrangement containing at least $3$ points contains two points with different colors. The source presents this as a stronger conjecture than the convex-set homothetic-copy statement and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Balázs Keszegh and Dömötör Pálvölgyi, “Proper Coloring of Geometric Hypergraphs”, arXiv:1612.02158 (2019).

record.title: The dual three-color pseudo-disk arrangement conjecture
record.statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a pseudo-disk arrangement, and let its members be the objects to be colored. **The dual pseudo-disk arrangement conjecture.** The members of any pseudo-disk arrangement admit a $3$-coloring such that every point contained in at least $3$ pseudo-disks is contained in two pseudo-disks with different colors. The source calls this the natural dual counterpart of the primal pseudo-disk arrangement conjecture and gives no resolution.
